known_before_registration: hybrid-shift-substitution (PR #35): combining boundary-shift (at its own established max capacity, nu_shift=1.0) with a small bigram-conditional substitution top-up (nu_sub) closed H1, H2, edge, and hapax all 20/20 at primary -- but token-order-share failed 0/20, a wide, consistent margin, reported as INVALID_CONSTRUCTION and not retuned, per that design's own precommitment

boundary-shift-novelty-null v1 vs v2 (PR #34 vs PR #36): v1's identical order-share failure was root-caused by reading the order-share metric's own code directly -- it collapses everything outside the 2,000 most frequent token types into one shared symbol before measuring token-to-token predictability, and v1's split-acceptance rule (both resulting pieces must be new) guaranteed two such collapsed tokens landed adjacent on every shift, manufacturing spurious predictability. v2 fixed this by preferring a split where exactly one piece is new (falling back to at-least-one-new, then to the unmodified pair, only when no such split exists). v2 passes all six criteria in 20/20 replicates.

checked directly in this design's own preregistration reasoning (not assumed): the hybrid script's boundary-shift component (data/scripts/external_hybrid_shift_substitution_novelty_null_audit.py, apply_boundary_shift) uses the ORIGINAL v1 split rule, not v2's fix -- confirmed by reading the code, and confirmed by commit order that hybrid (6d21635) was built and evaluated before v2 (188c5eb) existed. Hybrid's order-share failure was never re-tested against the v2 fix.

hypothesis under test, not yet verified: hybrid's order-share failure is the SAME bug already root-caused and fixed once in the standalone boundary-shift design, and swapping hybrid's split rule for the already-validated v2 rule (keeping everything else -- the substitution top-up, nu_shift=1.0, beta=0.5 -- unchanged) resolves it without reintroducing new problems
not_done_before_registration: No hybrid-v2 stream generated or scored
No parameter selected from any transformed outcome

nu_sub re-calibration (self-consistency-only, hapax-only, same methodology and candidate grid as the original hybrid design) not yet run -- nu_shift stays fixed at 1.0 (unchanged rationale: boundary-shift's own established maximum capacity, not re-tested as a free variable; the v2 split-rule change only affects WHICH split is chosen when a shift fires, not the shift trigger probability, so nu_shift=1.0 remains the right choice for the same reason it was chosen the first time)

claim: Swapping hybrid-shift-substitution's boundary-shift component for the already-validated v2 split rule (prefer a split where exactly one piece is new), keeping the substitution top-up, beta, and nu_shift unchanged, passes all six frozen criteria in at least 16 of 20 primary replicates.
honesty_precommitment: This is a high-prior-probability fix, not a guaranteed one: the exact bug already fixed once elsewhere may not be the full explanation for hybrid's order-share failure (the substitution top-up's own tokens, absent from the standalone boundary-shift design, could contribute a different or additional source of order predictability). If order-share still fails after this fix, or if fixing order breaks something the v1 hybrid passed (H1, H2, edge, hapax, all 20/20 at primary), that will be reported plainly as a new negative result, not retuned or reframed as a partial success.
base_mechanism: Naibbe cipher (voynich-units commit 956a7c4fc39981f4d116fa3f4edfccce6d065571) + identical boundary-coupling rule (beta=0.50 fixed, unchanged from every prior design).

representation.roundtrip_required: collapse(expand(atom)) == atom for every atomic_alphabet symbol

boundary_shift_v2_at_max_capacity.note: identical mechanics to boundary-shift-v2-novelty-null (PR #36) -- prefer a split where exactly one piece is new, fall back to at-least-one-new, then to the unmodified pair -- run at boundary-shift's own established maximum trigger rate (nu_shift is not re-tested as a free variable here, same rationale as the original hybrid design)

bigram_substitution_topup.eligibility: token is still a repeat of something already emitted AFTER the boundary-shift-v2 pass has run
bigram_substitution_topup.mechanism: identical single-atom bigram-conditional exhaustive substitution search used in bigram-novelty-null and the original hybrid design (same statistic, same sparse-context fallback, same cold-start rule, same protected position 0)
bigram_substitution_topup.note: unchanged from the original hybrid design -- only the boundary-shift component's split rule differs in this preregistration

primary.note: frozen from pilot: smallest grid value tested, clears the hapax floor (0.65) by a wide margin (pilot mean 0.9237) since v2's split rule saturates hapax far above the [0.65,0.75] target band the rule anticipated -- see selfreview.md pilot addendum for the disclosed deviation from the literal band

baseline.note: identical to boundary-state-null's baseline; not rerun, reused by reference

edge_only.note: identical to boundary-state-null's edge_only; not rerun, reused by reference

shift_only_no_topup.note: isolates how much of the primary's hapax comes from shift-v2 alone at this beta, for interpretation

configurations.pilot_calibration_rule: nu_sub chosen by a self-consistency-only pilot (3 seeds, hybrid_novelty_only config, beta=0, nu_shift=1.0 fixed) targeting hapax_share_of_types in [0.65, 0.75], selecting the SMALLEST nu_sub that lands in-band. Same candidate grid as the original hybrid design, reused unchanged rather than chosen fresh for this design: {0.01, 0.02, 0.03, 0.05, 0.08, 0.1}. Order-share is recorded during the pilot for information only and explicitly NOT used to select nu_sub, even if a different value looks more favorable on order in the pilot data -- selecting nu_sub to make order look better would be exactly the outcome-driven parameter selection this project's discipline forbids. This is the same rule as the original hybrid manifest, unchanged.

boundary.note: reused from boundary-state-null's edge_only vs baseline comparison, not recomputed

novelty.note: checked against hybrid_novelty_only (shift-v2+topup together, no coupling) vs baseline -- the full novelty mechanism for this design, not decomposed further, same convention as the original hybrid design

primary_verdict.pass: Both manipulation checks succeed and at least 16 of 20 primary replicates pass all six criteria
primary_verdict.fail: Both manipulation checks succeed and fewer than 16 of 20 primary replicates pass all six criteria

execution_embargo: Do not implement the transformation beyond the pilot-calibration step, or calculate any primary/control/sensitivity outcome, until the self-review pass documented in the accompanying log is complete.
